observation.visible_scene: A clear drinking glass holding water sits on a plain white surface, with a yellow-and-black STAEDTLER pencil propped inside it, leaning on the rim so that the part below the waterline looks displaced/bent relative to the part above. A human hand occupies the left foreground throughout the excerpt. A small green logo box is fixed in the upper-right corner. The glass and pencil remain in essentially the same position in every frame.
visible_changes: At the start (t=0–0.47s) the hand is held open with three fingers extended horizontally, fingertips pointing toward the left side of the glass, largely stationary.
Around t=0.53–0.67s the open hand drops and blurs out toward the lower-left, leaving the glass momentarily without a foreground hand.
From t=0.67s a single index finger re-enters from the bottom-left and moves up and to the right.

Between roughly t=0.8s and t=2.33s the index finger holds a pointing pose, its tip positioned in front of the glass aimed at the pencil near the waterline, with only small shifts of the fingertip along that region.
From t=2.4s to the end the pointing finger withdraws back toward the lower-left, becoming blurred as it moves away.
The pencil, glass, water level and apparent refraction bend stay unchanged; the visible motion is entirely from the hand/finger, not from the objects.
outside_clip_unknowns: What the person does before the excerpt begins and after it ends, and the purpose of the pointing gesture.
Whether the apparent break in the pencil is due to refraction or some other cause is not established by the clip alone.
uncertain_details: Exact finger identity of the pointing digit (looks like the index finger) is inferred from pose.
Minor jitter in framing may be hand-held camera motion or object motion; the background and glass position look stable, so camera movement is not clearly evidenced.
Blur in the transition frames is motion blur from the moving hand, not a cut or disappearance of the hand.
